Install tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms on Omarchy

This package builds the same DKMS kernel modules TUXEDO Computers ships for its laptops, covering function keys, keyboard backlight, fan control, power profiles, and other embedded-controller sensors, but with the hardware compatibility check disabled. That lets it run on laptops from other brands that share the same underlying barebone hardware as a supported TUXEDO model (for example a TUXEDO Pulse 14 Gen 4 and a rebadged Schenker Via 14 Pro). The maintainer warns this bypass can be risky since embedded-controller code that targets the wrong hardware can potentially cause damage.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 4.22.1-3:
    pacman -Qi tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms

Open and use tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms

tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms | grep /usr/bin/

tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms requirements and compatibility

  • A laptop whose hardware is identical or near-identical to a model TUXEDO's drivers already support (e.g. NB05/NB04/NB02, Sirius 16, or a rebadged equivalent from another brand)
  • DKMS and kernel headers for the running kernel

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • dkms

Free and open source. License: GPL-2.0-or-later.

Frequently asked questions

How do I install tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms. The download is 87.8 KB and it takes 441 KB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed GPL-2.0-or-later.

How do I uninstall tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms?

Run omarchy pkg drop tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms. It removes the package from your system.

What does tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms depend on?

The package declares 1 dependency: dkms. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms a desktop app?

No. tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as tuxedo-drivers-nocompatcheck-dkms (version 4.22.1-3) in the official Omarchy package repository. Martin Kröner makes it.
